incidente.resumo: After a blue/green database upgrade for the workflows service, all queries on the new database hit disk because the analyze operation that rebuilds its statistics table had run too early and was made stale by a second major version upgrade; customers saw increased latency and failures starting and canceling workflows and jobs. Service was restored by re-enabling writes on the old database and reinstating it as primary.

descricao.texto: At 22:17 UTC increased latency in the workflows service was identified, along with errors from jobs being dropped after exhausting their 10-minute retries.
trechos: At 22:17, we identified increased latency in the workflows service, as well as some errors from jobs being dropped due to exhausting their 10 minute retries.

descricao.texto: The analyze operation that rebuilds the database's statistics table, used for indexes, was executed too early in the upgrade and was made stale by a second major version upgrade within the same deployment, so all queries on the new database were hitting disk.
trechos: The root cause was determined to be that the analyze operation to rebuild the database’s statistics table, which is used for indexes, had been executed too early in the operation and was made stale by a second major version upgrade within the same deployment.
At 22:41, it was observed that all queries on the new database were hitting disk, which indicated that the database statistics tables had not updated.

descricao.texto: An upgrade to the service responsible for workflows, including a blue/green database deployment with a second major version upgrade within the same deployment.
trechos: At approximately 22:00 on April 4, we initiated an upgrade to the service responsible for workflows.
At 22:08, when the blue/green deployment was complete, we verified queries being served.

The root cause was determined to be that the analyze operation to rebuild the database’s statistics table, which is used for indexes, had been executed too early in the operation and was made stale by a second major version upgrade within the same deployment.

passos.texto: At 22:30 UTC the team restarted the workflows pods to ensure they were all connecting to the correct database.
trechos: At 22:29 additional engineers were engaged, and at 22:30 the team restarted the workflows pods to ensure they were all connecting to the correct database.

passos.texto: After observing that all queries on the new database were hitting disk, the team upsized the database and disabled non business critical operations on it.
trechos: At 22:41, it was observed that all queries on the new database were hitting disk, which indicated that the database statistics tables had not updated.
The team immediately upsized the database and disabled any non business critical operations on the database.

passos.texto: At 23:00 UTC the workflows service was scaled down to a single pod to give the database capacity to recover while the statistics table was rebuilt; by 23:10 the queue was backing up and database performance had not improved.
trechos: At 23:00, the workflows service was scaled down to a single pod to give the database capacity to recover while the statistics table was rebuilt.
At 23:10, the team observed the workflows queue backing up due to the reduction in pods as expected but also did not see an improvement in database performance.

passos.texto: At 23:19 UTC the team decided to re-enable writes on the old database and reinstate its primary status; this work completed at 23:29, and at 23:45 the workflow queue was back to normal levels with no further errors.
trechos: At 23:19, the team decided to re-enable writes on the old database and reinstate its primary status to restore service to customers sooner. This work completed at 23:29.
At 23:45 it was determined that the workflow queue was back to normal operating levels, and no further errors were observed.

acoes.texto: Already done: the blue/green database deployment procedures were updated to run an analysis procedure after every major version change.
trechos: The blue/green database deployment procedures have been updated to run an analysis procedure after every major version change.

acoes.texto: Already done: the team tested running the analyze command while a database is under pressure, to check that it has no further degrading effects on database performance; this will be noted for future remediation.
trechos: The team has also tested running the analyze command while a database is under pressure to determine it has no further degrading effects on the database performance. This will be noted for future remediation.

acoes.texto: Before any additional migrations, add automated tests and manual checkpoints throughout the process to identify and resolve issues before the blue/green cutover.
trechos: Before any additional migrations are run, the team will add additional automated tests and manual checkpoints throughout the process to identify and resolve issues before the blue/green cutover.
On April 3, 2025, from 22:08 UTC to 23:45 UTC, CircleCI customers experienced increased latency and some failures with starting and canceling workflows and jobs.

motivo_confianca_baixa: categoria_causa: database-storage vs other. The root cause is stale database statistics after an upgrade, leaving queries hitting disk; database-storage ('the datastore itself failed (limits, corruption, replication break)') fits a datastore problem but stale statistics is not one of its listed failure kinds, and no other category (configuration-error is about configuration, rules or policy; human-error about a wrong command, parameter or target) clearly covers an upgrade procedure step run too early, so 'other' also fits.
observacoes: The text gives two dates: the summary says April 3, 2025 (22:08 to 23:45 UTC) while the timeline says the upgrade started at approximately 22:00 on April 4; data_incidente is therefore given only as 2025-04. Duration (97 minutes) computed from the summary's stated start and end times.
